title: India's Bank Unions Signal Indefinite Strike Over 5-Day Week, PLI, and Pension Demands
excerpt: The United Forum of Bank Unions escalates its agitation after the government fails to implement a five-day work week agreed in the 2024 wage settlement, with PLI and pension updation adding to the standoff.
body:
• The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), representing nine unions across India's public sector banks, is escalating its agitation with threats of an indefinite strike over the government's failure to implement a five-day work week.
  • The five-day week was agreed during the 12th Bipartite Settlement with the Indian Banks' Association in March 2024, but the government has not issued the required notification under the Negotiable Instruments Act.
  • Additional flashpoints include the controversial Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for senior officers and the delayed updation of pension for retired bank employees.
  • Bank employees have staged black-badge protests and nationwide demonstrations, with union leaders warning of stronger actions if demands remain unaddressed.

A Promise Made, Not Kept

The standoff traces back to December 2023, when the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) and UFBU reached an agreement during wage negotiations to convert all remaining working Saturdays into holidays. The deal was formalised in the 12th Bipartite Settlement's joint note, signed on March 8, 2024. In exchange, bank employees agreed to work an additional 40 minutes each weekday — a trade-off that unions say would result in no net loss of working hours, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The IBA recommended the change to the government, which would need to amend the Negotiable Instruments Act to declare all Saturdays as bank holidays. More than two years later, the notification has not arrived.

Currently, banks remain open on the first, third, and fifth Saturdays of each month, while the Reserve Bank of India, Life Insurance Corporation, stock exchanges, and central and state government offices already operate on a five-day schedule.

From One-Day Strike to Indefinite Threat

UFBU's frustration has followed a steady escalation. In January 2026, the umbrella body called a one-day nationwide strike on January 27 after a conciliation meeting with the Chief Labour Commissioner failed to produce results. The strike disrupted branch-level services at 12 public sector banks, including State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, and Bank of Baroda, as reported by Amar Ujala.

"Despite detailed discussions during the conciliation proceedings, there was no assurance on our demand. Hence, we have been compelled to proceed with the strike action."

— C.H. Venkatachalam, General Secretary, All India Bank Employees Association

In March 2025, UFBU had deferred a planned two-day strike after receiving assurances from the Finance Ministry and IBA during a conciliation meeting. The Chief Labour Commissioner pledged to monitor the five-day banking issue directly and set April 22 as the next hearing date, Outlook Business reported. But unions say the assurances led nowhere.

By May 2026, the protest had taken a new form. Bank employees across the country wore black badges while working and staged lunchtime demonstrations outside branches, signalling deepening frustration, according to AnyTime News.

PLI and Pension Fuel the Fire

The five-day week is not the only grievance. The Department of Financial Services' directives on performance review and the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme — which applies to Scale-IV and above officers — have drawn sharp criticism from unions. UFBU leaders allege the PLI scheme is arbitrary, violates previously agreed terms from bipartite negotiations, and creates disparity among staff ranks.

Pension updation for retired bank employees is another unresolved demand. S. Nagarajan, General Secretary of the All India Bank Officers' Association, has said that pending staff service conditions agreed under bipartite wage negotiations — including the five-day week, PLI reform, and pension updation — must be implemented as a package, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Impact on Banking Services

Private sector banks, including HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank, remain unaffected by UFBU actions because their employees are not unionised under the forum. Digital banking channels — UPI, mobile banking, and internet banking — continue to function during strikes, though ATM cash availability can be strained in some areas due to logistical delays.

What Comes Next

Union leaders have made clear that failure to act on the five-day week, PLI withdrawal, and pension demands will trigger indefinite strike action. With the government showing no signs of issuing the required notification and multiple rounds of conciliation having produced only assurances, India's banking sector faces the prospect of prolonged disruption — unless the Finance Ministry breaks the deadlock.
nri_angle: NRIs who rely on Indian public sector banks for NRO/NRE accounts and cross-border transactions face service disruptions during strikes, while the broader standoff signals unresolved labour tensions in India's banking sector.
